content_preview.title: Robert Haas Attributes PostgreSQL 19's Late Release and Feature Reverts to LLM-Found Bugs, Citing a Jump of More Than 60% in Back-Patched Commits
content_preview.summary: In a post LWN linked on October 30, PostgreSQL developer Robert Haas says LLM-found bug reports drove more back-patching and late reverts; the project's own announcements give no cause.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Robert Haas, a PostgreSQL developer, has published a post titled "Postgres 19 is late, and it's AI's fault," in which he argues that bug reports found with large language models (LLMs) explain why PostgreSQL 19 is arriving later than recent major releases. LWN.net [linked to the post](https://lwn.net/Articles/1104210/) on October 30, 2026. The explanation is Haas's own account; the project's release announcements, discussed below, state no cause for the schedule change.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (806 words with link URLs stripped; writer counted 812; range 400-1200). Overview, What the Post Says, commit counts, mechanism, What the Project Has Announced, What We Don't Know. Clear attribution of everything to Haas; the limits of his inference are stated explicitly.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four gzipped snapshots from raw text and re-fetched all four live (text identical to snapshots). No suspicious_patterns on any source. source-0 (rhaas.blogspot.com, dated Fri Oct 30 2026, byline Robert Haas, 'Sr. Staff Software Engineer @ Databricks, PostgreSQL Major Contributor and Committer'; notes it originally appeared on neon.com): every quote verbatim ('no earlier than the middle of September, and no later than the middle of October'; 'most likely won't be released until November, and it's not impossible that the project could decide to postpone the release further'; reverts of FOR PORTION OF, SQL/PGQ, MERGE/SPLIT PARTITION 'between August 27 and September 15'; 'The short answer is that LLMs happened'; 'actually declined slightly'; 'jumped by more than 60%'; 'more than 74%'; 'It's possible that some of this jump...'; the two factors; 'particularly concerning'; 'Right now, I'm not sure'; 'scrutinized by AI'). Numbers are Haas's own: Apr 8-Sep 25: 2025 1037 master / 724 REL_18_STABLE; 2026 1443 master / 1169 REL_19_STABLE; 248 REL_17_STABLE (2025) vs 433 REL_18_STABLE (2026). The 60% figure is his (724 to 1169 is 61.5%, consistent); baseline = same date range one year earlier, branch-for-branch; he does not name the baseline as a percentage of anything else. Causation wording: Haas states 'LLMs happened' and 'I think that's also why we had so many late reverts, and why the release itself is delayed', calling the cause 'seems likely' for the commit jump; the title's 'Attributes ... to' and 'Citing' mirror his own framing, and the article correctly presents it as his inference rather than a measured breakdown. His role is stated in the article only as 'a PostgreSQL developer', within what the source says. source-1 (LWN 1104210, posted Oct 30 by corbet): links the Haas post by the identical URL and quotes its closing paragraphs; confirms the Oct 30 date claim. source-2 (Beta 4, posted 2026-09-24): RC 'should occur in early October', GA 'may also occur in October', 'strongly believes that, first and foremost, PostgreSQL must be reliable', and the reverts of SQL/PGQ, online checksums, FOR PORTION OF, MERGE/SPLIT PARTITIONS all present; no mention of LLMs. source-3 (RC 1, posted 2026-10-15): GA planned Nov 19, RC 2 Nov 12 with the update release that 'will include a large number of fixes', 'Unless an issue is discovered that requires a delay or an additional release candidate' all verbatim; no mention of LLMs or bug-report source. Check of the writer's statement that announcements give no cause: true for any LLM/AI cause. Precision note: Beta 4 does give a rationale for the reverts (reliability and more time in community development and review) and RC 1 gives the reason for RC 2 (fixes in the Nov 12 update release); the article reports both accurately in the body, so the Overview/summary phrasing 'no cause' is read as 'no cause identified for the underlying bug volume', which is acceptable, not a correction. Allowlist: rhaas.blogspot.com was not allowlisted. Authenticity independently verified: (1) LWN links to it by this exact URL, (2) the post is bylined Robert Haas with the Committer/Major Contributor tagline, (3) planet.postgresql.org (official community aggregator) lists this post under 'Robert Haas' linking to rhaas.blogspot.com, (4) live re-fetch matched the snapshot. Added to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment (maintainer-blog tier, precedent daniel.haxx.se); valid for Haas's own statements and measurements only. Commit counts were not independently checked against the git repository (the article says so; they are attributed to Haas throughout). Independence: sources 2-3 are first-party project announcements and LWN is an independent relay; the central claim rests on a single primary voice, stated as such.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All dates, counts, quotes and attributions verified individually against raw text; no fabricated specifics. Herald cross-links verified to exist and use the correct form: /article/2026-09/25-postgresql-19-beta-4-reverts-six-features-including-property-graph-queries-as-project-targets-an-october-release (News on Beta 4 reverts) and /article/2026-10/17-postgresql-19-rc-1-moves-general-availability-to-november-19-with-a-second-release-candidate-planned-for-november-12 (Briefing on RC 1 schedule); both described accurately. No orphan URLs: every body URL is in article.sources and vice versa.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Haas's opinions and the single-voice nature of the claim are flagged; no blame beyond the sources, no editorializing about the open-source project.
editor_notes.originality: New angle: the primary Haas post with his commit counts. Existing Herald coverage is the Beta 4 (Sep 25) and RC 1 (Oct 17) articles, which this extends and links. Overlap with PR #2749 (Analysis on PostgreSQL 19's delay, curl's open reporting and Edge's review automation, reviewed separately): that piece deliberately did not cite the blog and relays Haas via Phoronix and an earlier LWN item; it states 'None of the cited reports quantifies the share of delay attributable to LLM-found bugs'. No contradiction: this article supplies Haas's own commit counts, which are a measurement of back-patching, not of the share of delay, and says explicitly that the link to LLM use is his inference. Its quoted Haas factors (fix-review time, back-branch diversion) match the primary text. Reviewer of #2749 should note that Haas's blog is now allowlisted and that the two pieces are consistent; #2749 also cites an August LWN item where Haas questioned a simple LLM explanation, which is a different time point and not contradicted here.
concerns: Central claim rests on one named voice (Haas) and commit counts not independently checked against the repository; the article states both limits clearly.
Overview/summary 'state no cause for the schedule change' is slightly broader than the announcements (RC 1 explains RC 2 by pending fixes); body reports this accurately.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully hedged coverage of a primary-source claim by a named PostgreSQL committer, with verbatim quotes and correctly attributed numbers; no corrections needed. Featured candidacy: 2 - a major open-source database's late release attributed by its own committer to LLM-found bugs, with concrete back-patching figures of interest to a broad developer audience
